text: Every RAG system has two phases that run at completely different times. Ingestion happens ahead of time: chunk your documents, embed them, store the vectors. Query time happens the instant a user asks a question, and it needs to be fast.

Ingestion isn't something a user waits on. You take your documents, split them into smaller chunks, convert each chunk into a vector, and store those vectors in a vector database, each one tagged with its original text and useful metadata like date or source.

Query time is five steps: the user asks a question, you embed that question with the same model used at ingestion, the vector database retrieves the top-k closest chunks, those chunks get assembled into a prompt with the question, and the LLM generates an answer grounded in that real retrieved text.

Compare this to the ungrounded vendor-contract guess from lesson one. With retrieval in place, the actual clause from the actual contract gets pulled back and handed to the model — so the answer quotes something really in front of it, not a plausible-sounding guess.

Two pieces here — the embedding model and the vector database — are the foundation everything else depends on. That's exactly why the next two chapters go deep on each one before chapter four builds the full pipeline around them.
